title: Observability: token/KV metrics + tracing spans, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: production teams need finer-grained visibility into per-request token cost, KV cache behavior, and end-to-end latency so we can correlate cost regressions with model rollouts and infrastructure changes. This PR adds token-level cost/latency metrics, KV cache hit/miss tracing spans, updated Grafana dashboards, and tuned alert rules aimed at reducing noisy alerts while catching real regressions.

What changed (high level):
- Export new Prometheus metrics: redwood_token_cost_per_request, redwood_token_latency_p50/p90/p99, redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_misses_total, redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio (derived).
- Emit tracing spans around KV cache lookup/hit/miss with tags: model, route, key_bucket, cache_ttl_ms to allow upstream span joins.
- Updated Grafana dashboard: dashboards/token-kv-metrics.json includes per-model cost/latency breakdown, KV hit-ratio heatmap, and request-sample drilldowns.
- Alert tuning: consolidated token-cost regression alerts into two signals (per-model p90 token latency increase > 20% sustained 10m; per-route token-cost increase > 30% sustained 15m) and added adaptive suppression if cache hit ratio drops (to avoid alert storms during cache warmup).
- Prometheus scrape: added exporter labels and improved cardinality controls (route -> route_group mapping).
- Tests: unit tests for metrics formatting and an integration test that exercises tracing spans and validates metrics emitted for synthetic traffic.

Why this approach: token-level metrics let us attribute cost regressions to either model or serving inefficiencies. KV tracing helps diagnose cold-start and cache-eviction-related cost increases. Dashboards are organized by workload so SREs and product owners can quickly pivot from a cost spike to the offending model/route.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to prod clusters over 2 weeks: enable metrics + tracing in canary region, run synthetic load for 24h, validate no cardinality explosion, then enable in remaining regions. Alert rules applied to non-prod first, then promoted.

Follow-ups: implement automated rollback for model rollouts that trigger token-cost alerts (ENG-7488), add sampling controls to tracing for high-traffic routes, and surface sample request payloads in the UI for easier triage.

release_notes: Observability: add token-level cost and latency metrics (per-request) to attribute cost to models and routes.
Tracing: emit KV cache spans to help debug cache misses and cold-starts.
Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard 'Token + KV metrics' for cost/latency and cache hit-ratio visibility.
Alerts: tuned token-cost and latency alerts to reduce noise and added adaptive suppression during cache warmup.
